questions.q: What information does collaborative filtering use to make recommendations?
options: Item descriptions and categories
The text of user reviews only
Which users interacted with which items, from the user-item matrix
The price of each item
questions.explain: Collaborative filtering uses only the interaction patterns in the user-item matrix. Item attributes are what content-based methods use.

questions.q: In the lesson, item 0 had cosine similarity 0.52 with item 1 and 0.29 with item 20. What does this tell you?
options: Item 0 and item 1 were clicked by more of the same users, matching the built-in taste groups
Item 20 is a better recommendation for every user
Cosine similarity is only valid between items in different groups
The similarity matrix must contain a mistake
questions.explain: Higher cosine similarity means more overlap in the users who clicked both items. Items 0 and 1 share a taste group; item 20 belongs to the other.

questions.q: What does the line scores = clicks @ item_sim compute for each user and candidate item?
options: The item's average rating
The sum of the candidate item's similarities to the items that user has already clicked
The number of users who clicked the item
The distance between two users
questions.explain: Multiplying the click matrix by the item-similarity matrix adds up, for each candidate item, its similarity to every item the user clicked.

questions.q: What does TruncatedSVD with n_components=2 do to the click matrix in the lesson?
options: Deletes all but two users
Keeps only the two most popular items
Predicts star ratings for two new items
Compresses each user into two latent factors and reconstructs scores for the empty cells from them
questions.explain: Matrix factorization describes users (and items) with a few latent factors, then multiplies them back together to score every user-item pair, including unseen ones.

questions.q: A retailer adds a brand-new product with zero clicks. Why does pure collaborative filtering struggle to recommend it?
options: Cosine similarity cannot be computed for products
SVD requires exactly 30 items
New products are always unpopular by definition
With no interactions, the item has no column of clicks to compare with other items
questions.explain: This is the cold-start problem: collaborative methods need interaction history, so a new item has nothing to be similar to until users click it.
